decision_points.question: which covariates/controls enter the adjustment model?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival specification of the control set for the primary skin-tone regression; an analyst commits to one column set, so they are mutually exclusive answers to what gets adjusted for (the near-default logistic link and binary skin tone embedded in some of these are held constant across the group)

decision_points.question: which regression family/estimator relates skin tone to red cards?
decision_points.why_rival: risk-difference, OLS/linear, Poisson-with-offset, and Poisson GLMM are alternative estimators for the same outcome; the primary model is fit with exactly one family

decision_points.question: how are records with missing height/weight (and bias) covariates handled — imputed or dropped?
decision_points.why_rival: each disposes of records lacking covariate values a different way — mean/median/zero imputation versus complete-case restriction — and imputing precludes dropping the same rows

decision_points.question: are dyads with implausible, out-of-range physical measurements excluded?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option settling whether measured-but-implausible height/weight values are filtered out (distinct from missing-value handling, since these rows have measurements)

decision_points.question: how are standard errors and model inference estimated (clustering unit, robust variance, weighting)?
decision_points.why_rival: unclustered ML, player-clustered, referee/refCountry-clustered, HC1, HC3, and games-weighted variance are competing inference procedures for one primary fit; an analyst selects one

decision_points.question: how are the physical/adjustment covariates transformed or encoded before entering the model?
decision_points.why_rival: deriving BMI, adding quadratic body-size terms, or z-scoring/log/bucket encoding are alternative functional-form representations of the same covariates

decision_points.question: is a skin-tone × league interaction included so the effect can vary by league?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option settling whether effect heterogeneity across leagues is modeled via an interaction term versus a single pooled effect

decision_points.question: is a multicollinearity (VIF) diagnostic applied to screen the covariates?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option settling whether a VIF collinearity check is run as a covariate-screening step

decision_points.question: what descriptive summary of the sample is produced?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option settling the descriptive/summary-table reporting step, separate from any inferential modeling choice
